claim_summary: AnomaMind contributes an anomaly-specific sequential agent workflow that combines learned interval decisions with tool-based evidence construction and iterative refinement.

claim_evidence.quote: Crucially, AnomaMind adopts a hybrid inference mechanism: general-purpose models handle tool invocation and self-reflective refinement, while a detection-specific policy is optimized through rule-based rewards that encourage valid parsing, F1-score alignment, and false-positive control.

modules.name: Coarse-to-fine anomaly workflow
modules.scope_reason: R3_1 TSK applies because the stages produce anomaly interval decisions and organize anomaly evidence; if the family changed, the candidate-interval actions and anomaly decision objective would need redesign. The workflow uses temporal intervals, but its core is bound to anomaly detection, so it fails the task-independent GTS counterfactual.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:yes - anomaly interval decisions and evidence workflow
R4:Planning and Orchestration; Tools and Execution

evidence.quote: AnomaMind instantiates the general process as a structured coarse-to-fine workflow. The workflow is organized into four implementation stages, each corresponding to one role in Table I:
Table I: coarse evidence acquisition by the locator, adaptive evidence construction by the actor, anomaly detection by the detector, and iterative refinement by the evaluator.
AnomaMind further incorporates an iterative refinement mechanism to evaluate and revise detection outcomes when necessary.

modules.name: Anomaly detector SFT and reinforcement learning
modules.scope_reason: R2 places this policy on the LLM side because it trains the model to produce interval-level anomaly decisions. R3 does not apply; the module is not harness code, and changing the task requires changing its anomaly-specific decision objective.

evidence.quote: we conduct supervised fine-tuning to initialize the detection-specific policy with anomaly reasoning traces. This stage teaches the detector to interpret diagnostic context and generate interval-level outputs,
while the RL stage further optimizes decision quality using parsing, F1-score, and false-positive rewards.

modules.name: Anomaly pattern and domain knowledge memory
modules.scope_reason: R3_1 TSK does not apply to the memory mechanism itself: it retrieves contextual knowledge and pattern prototypes rather than implementing the anomaly output objective or verifier. Its temporal anomaly examples make it GTS; the retrieval and retained-context structure could be reused for another task with different contents, so the task-change counterfactual does not require redesigning its temporal memory mechanism.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:no - memory supplies context but does not decide anomaly labels
R3_2_GTS:yes - retains and retrieves temporal pattern context
